dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a measure μ and real-valued functions X,Y, this is ∫(X(ω)−∫X dμ)(Y(ω)−∫Y dμ) dμ, the centered mixed second moment (covariance under a probability measure).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the real number inside the norm on the left-hand side.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For μ and X, this is the nonnegative real square root of LocalDef004 μ X, hence the square root of X's centered second moment.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Applied to X and Y, it supplies the two factors multiplied on the right-hand side.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: Maps a real-valued function X to its Bochner/Lebesgue integral ∫X dμ; on a probability space this is its expectation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms the means of X and Y, the centered-product integral, and the centered-square integrals occurring through D001 and D004.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: For μ and X, this is ∫(X(ω)−∫X dμ)^2 dμ, the centered second moment (variance under a probability measure).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Its square root defines each D002 factor on the right-hand side.

binders: An arbitrary type Ω equipped with a measurable-space structure.
An arbitrary measure μ on Ω equipped with an IsProbabilityMeasure instance, so μ is a probability measure.
hypotheses: X satisfies MemLp X 2 μ: it is almost-everywhere strongly measurable and has finite L² seminorm with respect to μ.
Y satisfies MemLp Y 2 μ: it is almost-everywhere strongly measurable and has finite L² seminorm with respect to μ.
conclusions: The absolute value of ∫(X(ω)−∫X dμ)(Y(ω)−∫Y dμ) dμ is at most sqrt(∫(X(ω)−∫X dμ)^2 dμ) multiplied by sqrt(∫(Y(ω)−∫Y dμ)^2 dμ).
mathematical_definitions: Define the centered mixed second moment Covμ(X,Y)=∫(X−Eμ[X])(Y−Eμ[Y]) dμ.
Define the centered second moment Varμ(X)=∫(X−Eμ[X])² dμ and similarly for Y.
Define σμ(X)=sqrt(Varμ(X)) and σμ(Y)=sqrt(Varμ(Y)), using the nonnegative real square root.
The norm of a real number is its absolute value.
translation.proposition_plain_english: On any probability space, for any two real-valued square-integrable functions X and Y, the absolute value of their centered mixed second moment (their covariance) is at most the product of the square roots of their centered second moments (their standard deviations): |Covμ(X,Y)|≤σμ(X)σμ(Y).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The result is restricted to real-valued functions and to measures carrying a probability-measure instance.
Both functions must satisfy the precise MemLp exponent-2 hypotheses; for functions failing either premise, the implication is vacuously true.
The target quantifies over raw functions Ω→ℝ rather than L² equivalence classes, although the integral and MemLp conditions are insensitive to almost-everywhere modification in the usual way.
No independence, identical-distribution, centering, or zero-mean assumption is imposed; centering is performed inside the definitions.
The local definitions use the direct centered-integral formulas rather than separately asserting an algebraically equivalent formula such as E[XY]−E[X]E[Y].
The target does not state equality conditions, strictness conditions, or a converse.
Real.sqrt is a total function, but under the L² hypotheses each displayed centered-square integral has its usual nonnegative variance interpretation.
Because MemLp is an implication premise, the theorem itself does not assert that arbitrary real-valued functions are measurable or integrable.
